representation: skeptic/1.0; numerical audit only, excluded from comparable physics distances

scopedClaim.claim: All 28 supplied candidates are marked valid, with reported eigen residuals and unitarity errors near double-precision roundoff and modest reported maximum condition values. These diagnostics support internal numerical consistency of the reported toy responses under their unspecified definitions. They neither establish scientific novelty nor identify a physical transport mechanism.

preserved: Per-candidate eigenResidual, unitarityError, maxCondition and validity flag.
Reported solver consistency, approximate probability-conservation diagnostic and conditioning summary.
All 28 descriptor-registry candidate identifiers and the registry statement that responses are numerically valid toy responses, not global novelty.
informationLost: Hamiltonians, scattering matrices, eigenvectors, energy grids, physical parameterization and transport observables are absent.
Residual normalization, matrix norm, condition-number definition, validity tolerances, solver algorithm, working precision and convergence histories are absent.
Reported maxima do not reveal where conditioning peaks or whether an energy grid misses a narrow resonance.
These four diagnostics cannot identify topology, mechanisms, material realizations, novelty, chemistry, Kagome physics, mechanical stress or hysteresis.

limitations: Every supplied observation contains all four expected metrics; completeness here concerns only this packet, not omitted simulator states or external evidence.
Near-roundoff residuals suggest numerical consistency but cannot certify forward accuracy without normalization, conditioning definitions and reference calculations.
valid=true is a supplied flag; its acceptance rule was not available for independent verification.
Tiny differences among residuals are not physical dissimilarity and should not rank novelty or transport behavior.
No uncertainty intervals, independent implementation, model-error estimate, discretization checks or experimental validation are supplied.
Procedural isolation is not statistical independence; the simulator and curated pool remain shared.

proposedTest.question: For all 28 exact archived toy inputs, does an independent higher-precision recomputation reproduce the scattering matrices and eigenvalues across a refined energy grid while satisfying explicitly normalized residual and unitarity tolerances?
proposedTest.control: Retrieve the exact simulator inputs and metric definitions first; use the same Hamiltonian and lead conventions in an independently implemented solver at at least 80 decimal digits. Include an analytically solvable Hermitian scattering case and a deliberately perturbed nonunitary scattering matrix to verify the diagnostic detects a known violation. Compare eigenvalue sets without relying on eigenvector ordering, and compare scattering matrices using the same channel phase convention. Record the original and refined energy grids.
proposedTest.failureCriterion: Flag numerical certification as failed or incomplete if any archived input or normalization is unavailable, a control fails, a dimensionless normalized eigen residual or relative Frobenius unitarity defect exceeds 1e-10, or the independently recomputed scattering matrix or matched eigenvalue set differs from the original by more than 1e-8 under documented relative scaling. These are proposed audit thresholds, not inferred original validity rules. A failure challenges numerical robustness or reproducibility; a pass does not establish novelty or implementation mechanism.
